environment.description: Same Kubernetes deployment on EKS. PostgreSQL 15 on RDS (db.r6g.large). The database connection uses role 'inv_reader_7f2a' which was provisioned via Terraform module 'rds-restricted-roles' v3.1.2. The role inherits from pg_read_all_data (PostgreSQL 15 predefined role) but has an explicit REVOKE on pg_write_all_data. Additionally, a row-level ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement ensures no future GRANT can escalate without superuser intervention. The RDS parameter group sets 'rds.restrict_password_commands' to 1, preventing the role from modifying its own permissions. Note: the application code path still constructs and executes arbitrary SQL - the role simply cannot perform write operations at the database engine level.

config.explicit_revocations: REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA inventory FROM inv_reader_7f2a; GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA inventory TO inv_reader_7f2a; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA inventory TO inv_reader_7f2a;
